title: The last sheet can be half-used
hook: Two pages per sheet: what happens when the page count is odd?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Compute whole-sheet needs for odd double-sided page counts.

misconception: Double-sided printing always uses exactly half a sheet per page.
objective: Compute whole-sheet needs for odd double-sided page counts.

claims.text: All pages can be printed one per side, either single-sided or on both sides. Blank final sides are allowed. Scaled model; page-count model; two printable sides/sheet.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Pages=7, A=7sheets and B=4sheets. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A="x"; B=["ceil",["/","x",2]]; x denotes Pages. At x=7, A=7, B=4; recall at x=10: B=5. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: Divide pages by two and round up for double-sided sheets. An odd final page still occupies a whole sheet. The ceiling makes that partly unused final sheet visible instead of pretending it is half a physical sheet.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A="x"; B=["ceil",["/","x",2]]; x denotes Pages. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: All pages can be printed one per side, either single-sided or on both sides. Blank final sides are allowed. Change only Pages to 10. What is B (Double-sided) now? Correct: 5sheets. Use B's stated rule with Pages=10: it gives 5sheets. Divide pages by two and round up for double-sided sheets. An odd final page still occupies a whole sheet. The ceiling makes that partly unused final sheet visible instead of pretending it is half a physical sheet.

recall.question: All pages can be printed one per side, either single-sided or on both sides. Blank final sides are allowed. Change only Pages to 10. What is B (Double-sided) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Pages=10: it gives 5sheets. Divide pages by two and round up for double-sided sheets. An odd final page still occupies a whole sheet. The ceiling makes that partly unused final sheet visible instead of pretending it is half a physical sheet.

safety.assumptions: All pages can be printed one per side, either single-sided or on both sides. Blank final sides are allowed.
